title: Northbridge Capital - Dedicated capacity discovery
topics: reserved GPU sizing and burst strategy
summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood Dedicated for low-latency, high-throughput inference for Northbridge's portfolio of financial NLP models. Key concerns: isolation/data residency, predictable throughput during market spikes, burst handling, and SSO/KMS integrations. Next steps: send sizing options, pricing tiers, security docs, and schedule a POC benchmark window.
action_items: Jordan Blake: share Dedicated SKUs, pricing tiers, and reserved capacity templates by 2026-03-06
Priya Nair: propose benchmark plan (sample prompts + metrics) and availability for a 2-week POC by 2026-03-09
Maya Chen: provide representative workloads and token distribution CSV by 2026-03-08
Lina Gomez: request for SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs - Redwood to share link by 2026-03-06
next_steps: Redwood to send Dedicated pricing and capacity options
Customer to send sample traffic and token distribution
Schedule POC benchmark window (tentative week of 2026-03-16)
Follow-up meeting to review benchmark plan and SLAs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Head of ML, Northbridge), Alex Rivera (CTO), Evan Park (Infra Lead), Lina Gomez (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. I'm Jordan Blake, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya our SE and Sam from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya: Doing well, thanks. Thanks for making time. We're pretty excited to understand how Dedicated works, particularly around reserved GPUs and how you handle bursts during market events.
[00:15] Jordan: Great, that's exactly what we planned to cover. Priya do you want to run the agenda?
[00:20] Priya: Yeah sure, quick agenda - current infra and constraints, workloads and traffic patterns, dedicated capacity sizing, burst and autoscale behaviour, security/compliance questions, and then wrap with next steps.
[00:30] Alex: Quick note - our timeline is fairly aggressive, target pilot in mid-March if possible.
[00:34] Jordan: Noted. We'll try to be pragmatic.
[00:38] Priya: Maya, can you give us a quick overview of the stack and models you plan to serve?
[00:43] Maya: Yeah, sure. We run a couple of transformer models — two main ones. A smaller 7B model for low-latency routing and a 13B model for higher quality summarization. Both are fine-tuned on internal financial docs. Right now those are on prem with a combination of dedicated hosts and some cloud spot capacity — which has been hit or miss during end-of-day spikes.
[01:05] Evan: To add, our existing infra is Kubernetes on GCE, we have HPA for our microservices but model hosts are more stateful, we've been managing model servers ourselves with a homegrown sharding + cache approach. We're interested in offloading the inference serving.
[01:18] Priya: Understandable. For Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools — customers get isolation and predictable throughput. Sizing depends on peak concurrency and latency SLOs; curious what your p50/p95 token latency targets are?
[01:32] Maya: For the 7B we want p95 under 150ms ideally; for 13B p95 under 400-500ms is OK for batchy summarization but p50 should be around 200ms. Token-level latency is important because some of our features are interactive.
[01:46] Priya: Got it. Are you doing streaming responses or full response generation?
[01:50] Maya: Both. Chat features need streaming. Summaries can be full responses.
[01:54] Jordan: On burst behavior — Priya, can you explain Redwood's burst and autoscale options for Dedicated?
[02:00] Priya: Yes. Dedicated has reserved GPUs sized for committed throughput and we offer a burst pool that can be used when reserved capacity is saturated. Burst is metered differently and subject to available capacity regionally; there's also an option for burst banking where you pre-purchase a buffer. We can also configure autoscale policies — scale on queue length or latency signals — but there are tradeoffs with cold start KV-cache warmups for large models.
[02:22] Evan: That warmup bit is big for us; cold starts kill latency for some RTT-sensitive flows. How long does warmup typically take?
[02:29] Priya: For large models with KV warmup, depending on sequence length and architecture, warmup can be 10-60s to fully warm caches if the model wasn't recently used. We mitigate this with continuous prefilling and smart routing to keep hot shards warm; for Dedicated we can pin warm instances to avoid cold starts but that increases committed cost.
[02:45] Maya: We're OK spending for predictability but want to understand cost math — what's the delta between reserved-only vs reserved+burst?
[02:53] Jordan: We'll send a breakdown but ballpark, reserved-only priced per month per GPU, burst usage billed at a higher per-minute rate. Commitment discounts apply for 6-12 month contracts. We'll include examples based on your traffic shape.
[03:06] Alex: On the isolation front, do we get a VPC and private networking with Dedicated? Data residency?
[03:12] Priya: Yes, Dedicated comes with VPC peering or PrivateLink-style connectivity, customer-managed networking. For Private deployments we have full on-prem or VPC-hosted control plane options as well. Audit logs and KMS integration supported.
[03:23] Lina: On KMS we need HSM-backed keys and a clear description of where logs live, retention, and access controls. SOC2 plus some ISO questions.
[03:32] Priya: We are SOC2 Type II; we have documented KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM via BYOK). We'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:41] Evan: Are you able to run in our GCP region? We need low network hops to our data stores.
[03:47] Jordan: We have regional capacity across major clouds — we can check specific availability in your preferred zone and list GPU types.
[03:53] Maya: Traffic patterns — our baseline QPS is around 40 req/s during trading hours, spiking up to 900 req/s for short 5-10 minute windows around market events. Token sizes vary widely — median 60 tokens, 95th 450 tokens.
[04:12] Priya: That's helpful. For that pattern we'd probably suggest a baseline reserved pool sized for sustained QPS and a burst pool to absorb spikes. The question is how many concurrent model calls — do you multiplex a single request across shards or is each request single-session?
[04:24] Evan: Each request maps to a single session/VM; we do some batching at the app layer but not always.
[04:29] Priya: In that case we can size to concurrency. For example, if 900 req/s with average latency 200ms that's roughly 180 concurrent slots peak. Depending on model throughput per GPU we can recommend number of GPUs; for 7B we typically see X tokens/s per A100 equiv, the 13B is lower. We'll do a quick calc in the sizing sheet.
[04:46] Jordan: We'll also propose a split — mix of lower-quantized instances for cost efficiency and some FP16 or higher perf instances to keep interactive latency low.
[04:55] Alex: Speaking of quantization, do you manage quantized builds or do we bring our own artifacts?
[04:59] Priya: We have a model onboarding flow. We can accept your fine-tuned weights and handle quantization and tuning for the Dedicated runtime, but customers can also provide pre-quantized artifacts. We validate performance and LL metrics during onboarding.
[05:12] Maya: What's the rollback story if a quantized variant degrades quality?
[05:16] Priya: We support A/B and canary rollouts across Dedicated pools; we also keep model version pinning and quick fallback to FP16 variants if regressions occur. We'll enable quality checks tied to your prompt suite as part of the POC.
[05:29] Evan: For our security people, can Redwood restrict access to CLIs and control plane with SAML/SSO and RBAC?
[05:36] Jordan: Yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC are available for Dedicated and Private customers.
[05:42] Lina: Also need IP allowlists, audit trails, and signed request logs.
[05:46] Priya: Audit trails and request-level logging are supported; we can discuss retention windows and exporting logs to your SIEM.
[05:53] Maya: Latency SLA? We need guarantees around p95 latency for the interactive routes.
[05:58] Jordan: For Dedicated we can commit to latency SLOs in contractual SLAs for reserved pools, subject to model and prompt shape. We'll surface SLO calculations and targets in the proposal.
[06:10] Alex: Let's talk about failure modes — if regional capacity is exhausted and burst can't be fulfilled, what happens?
[06:16] Priya: Outages: Redwood supports fallback routing rules — we can route to secondary region or to hosted model variants (lower-cost) depending on your policy. For strict isolation customers may prefer multi-region Dedicated pools. We also support queueing policies to shed non-critical requests.
[06:31] Evan: How quickly can you spin up more capacity? If we want to scale from 20 to 80 GPUs in a day, is that feasible?
[06:38] Priya: Usually we can schedule capacity growth in hours to a day depending on cloud provider allocations; for very fast increases we rely on burst pools or pre-negotiated capacity windows. If you need instant elastic to 4x, you'd want a burst banking arrangement or pre-reserved extra.
[06:52] Maya: For cost reasons we can't pre-reserve 4x throughput all the time. We need a predictable burst plan that doesn't blow the budget.
[06:58] Jordan: We'll model an example where reserved covers baseline and a capped burst bank covers expected spike volume per month with a price ceiling.
[07:06] Alex: Can you show us historical customer patterns where burst banking saved cost versus overprovisioning?
[07:12] Priya: We'll include anonymized examples in the sizing doc; high-frequency trading-like customers often save 30-50% by using reserved plus burst banking vs always running peaked capacity.
[07:22] Maya: On observability, do we get token-level costing and per-route dashboards? We need cost attribution to teams.
[07:29] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-model and per-route dashboards, per-request traces, and can export billing into your cost analytics.
[07:38] Lina: About data retention — do logs or payloads ever leave the VPC? We need to prove no consumer data persists in Redwood storage.
[07:45] Priya: For Dedicated with VPC peering, logs stay in your account or can be exported to your storage. We provide options to disable long-term payload retention; ephemeral telemetry can be sampled.
[07:56] Evan: Are there examples of customers with similar regulatory constraints?
[07:59] Jordan: Yes, financial customers on Dedicated/Private — we'll share case studies and references upon NDA.
[08:06] Maya: If we do a POC, what's the minimal footprint? Can we test just the 7B interactive route?
[08:12] Priya: Absolutely. A scoped POC for the 7B interactive path is common — we'd run a 2-week benchmark, measure p50/p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and run stress tests on spikes.
[08:23] Maya: Sounds good. For the benchmark we'll want to replay production traces, can you ingest those?
[08:27] Priya: Yes, we can accept anonymized traces and micro-benchmarks. We'll need prompt sets and token distribution to make the sizing realistic.
[08:34] Jordan: Let's talk timelines — Priya, what's your availability to run a POC mid-month?
[08:39] Priya: I have bandwidth starting 2026-03-16 for a 2-week window. We can schedule capacity and get security docs before then.
[08:46] Alex: Great, we aim for the same window.
[08:49] Maya: A couple of specific questions — SLIs to measure during POC, and role-based access for read-only ops.
[08:56] Priya: SLIs: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, cold-start rate, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens. RBAC: yes, we can create read-only roles and restrict deploy permissions.
[09:06] Evan: Regarding networking, we need to ensure egress flows and firewall rules, do you have a network runbook?
[09:11] Jordan: We'll attach our network runbook and example firewall rules in the follow-up.
[09:16] Lina: Also want to confirm retention and encryption of model artifacts at rest.
[09:20] Priya: Models at rest are encrypted with customer-managed KMS where required. We'll document where keys live and rotation options.
[09:27] Maya: Pricing again — can you give a rough estimate now for a baseline? Say, baseline 10 GPUs reserved and potential burst of 30 GPUs for short windows.
[09:35] Jordan: Ballpark only — depends on GPU type and region. For A100-equivalent GPUs, reserved monthly rates with 12-month commitment might be in the low thousands per GPU per month; burst metering higher. We'll send concrete numbers in the proposal with your region and preferred GPU.
[09:50] Alex: Will we be able to run custom monitoring hooks and exporters? e.g., Prometheus endpoints?
[09:56] Priya: Yes, we support Prometheus metrics export and custom tracing hooks; you can plug into your observability stack.
[10:02] Maya: Ok, let's go through a little hypothetical sizing exercise live if that's ok.
[10:06] Priya: Yep, give me your baseline qps again and latency target for the interactive route.
[10:10] Maya: Baseline 40 req/s, p95 150ms for 7B. Peak 900 for 5-10 minutes.
[10:16] Priya: If we assume 150ms avg at p95, 40 req/s is about 6 concurrent slots sustained; that's small. Peaks at 900 req/s with 150ms equates to 135 concurrent slots. For 7B on an A100 equiv, we often see ~X concurrent sessions per GPU depending on batch size — let's assume 10-20 concurrent for low-latency config, so you'd need ~7-14 GPUs for baseline and then extra 7-14 for peaks. This is rough and we'll refine with traces.
[10:42] Evan: That aligns with our naive math.
[10:45] Jordan: We'll put these numbers in a spreadsheet and run a more precise calc.
[10:49] Alex: A few procurement questions — what's the minimum contract length and SLAs?
[10:54] Jordan: Minimum for Dedicated usually 3 months for small pilots but enterprise reserved commitments are 6-12 months with SLA add-ons. We'll outline options.
[11:02] Maya: Anything else on compliance? Lina any questions?
[11:06] Lina: Please include PCI-ish controls we have to check for financial info and also the ability for forensic logs on request.
[11:13] Priya: We'll include the compliance matrix.
[11:16] Jordan: Ok let's do recap and owners.
[11:18] Jordan: Action items recap: Jordan to share pricing and Dedicated SKUs, Priya to send benchmark plan and POC availability, Maya to send sample traces, Lina to request security docs (Redwood to provide). Any other items?
[11:29] Maya: Could you include an example contract with guaranteed capacities and exit clauses?
[11:33] Jordan: Yes we can provide a term sheet.
[11:36] Alex: We'll also loop in procurement after the sizing doc.
[11:39] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet, security pack, and propose POC dates. Thanks everyone.
[11:45] Maya: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:48] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional model names and acronyms incorrectly transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' appears as 'K V cache', 'PrivateLink' as 'private link'), some words run together — reflects typical Fireflies output.
